headline: Ghana Business Index Slips to 49.8 in October
summary: Ghana's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 49.8 in October 2026 from 51.3 in the previous month, signaling a contraction in business activity as it dropped below the 50-point threshold.
why: The PMI is a key economic indicator that measures the health of the manufacturing and services sectors; a reading below 50 indicates a contraction in economic activity.

impacts.name: Ghana
impacts.why: The PMI drop indicates a slowdown in the country's private sector business activity.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A decline in the PMI below 50 suggests a contraction in business conditions, which typically dampens investor sentiment regarding the country's short-term economic growth prospects.
